title: Stock Market Update: Slipping From Record Highs
text:
Slipping From Record Highs 29-Jan-18 13:00 ET Dow -85.87 at 26530.84, Nasdaq -15.02 at 7490.75, S&P -8.41 at 2864.46 
[BRIEFING.COM] Stocks have slipped from record highs today as investors take some money off the table ahead of a busy week. 
The S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and the Nasdaq Composite hold losses of around 0.3% apiece and have traded within a pretty narrow range throughout the session. The small-cap Russell 2000 trades roughly in line with the three major stock indices, down 0.4%. 
Market participants have a lot on their plates this week: President Trump is set to deliver his first State of the Union address on Tuesday, the Federal Open Market Committee will release its latest policy directive--the final policy directive under the leadership of Janet Yellen--on Wednesday,   (Briefing.com consensus 180K) will cross the wires on Friday, and, scattered throughout, heavyweights like Apple (AAPL 168.51, -3.00), Microsoft (MSFT 93.91, -0.14), Facebook (FB 187.51, -2.47), Alphabet (GOOGL 1190.64, +3.08), Amazon (AMZN 1418.23, +16.18), Boeing (BA 340.48, -2.74), and others will report their quarterly results. 
With so many potentially market-moving events on radar, investors have dialed back their bullish tone today and have sent the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX 13.00, +1.93) higher by 17.4%. However, it would not be surprising to see the bulls buy the intraday dip and make a late-afternoon run into record territory as they've so often done in the recent past. 
U.S. Treasuries have sold off today, but they have come up from their overnight lows. The yield on the benchmark 10-yr Treasury note is up four basis points at 2.70% after hovering around 2.72% earlier. Meanwhile, the 2-yr yield is up one basis point at 2.13%. Yields move inversely to prices. 
The rate-sensitive utilities (-1.1%) and real estate (-1.2%) sectors have stayed at the back of the pack due to the increase in Treasury yields, while the heavily-weighted financial sector (-0.1%) has outperformed, boosted by the steepening of the yield curve--and the prospect of higher profit margins that accompany it. 
Apple has struggled, losing 1.7%, following a weekend report from the Nikkei Asian Review that   by 50% in the first quarter following a disappointing holiday season. Apple's negative performance has weighed on the technology sector, which is down 0.6%. 
In other corporate news, Dr Pepper Snapple (DPS 118.80, +23.21) has spiked 24.2%   
On the earnings front, Lockheed Martin (LMT 348.85, +3.95) and Seagate Tech (STX 54.82, -0.12) both reported better-than-expected earnings and revenues this morning, but are trading mixed; LMT shares are up 1.2% while STX shares are lower by 0.2%. LMT   
Also of note, VMware (VMW 135.39, -14.61), a subsidiary of Dell, has dropped 9.8%--giving back Friday's big gain--after CNBC tweeted that Dell is considering selling the software company. On Friday, VMW shares rallied 9.0% following a Wall Street Journal report that Dell is exploring options regarding VMware.
